candidates.title: The Chair Outside The Door
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu goes quiet behind a closed door and worries that silence makes her hard to love; Zuv proves he understands by staying near without forcing the explanation.
candidates.emotional_truth: Some people are not asking to be decoded immediately. They are asking not to be abandoned while they become speakable again.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The person who shuts down after being overwhelmed, then feels guilty because even needing space feels like a burden.
candidates.visual_evidence: A closed bedroom or bathroom door; a glass of water and phone charger left outside; one chair pulled close to the door; Zuv's presence shown by his slippers, hand, or shadow rather than forcing his face into every frame; later, the door slightly open and the untouched glass now half empty.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium if it becomes 'he waited for her' as a noble speech. It stays sharp only if the love is shown through the exact objects left at the door and the restraint of not demanding a conversation.

candidates.title: The Third Are You Mad?
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu asks 'are you mad?' for the third time in one evening, and the answer is not a dramatic reassurance; it is Zuv changing the room so her nervous system can believe him.
candidates.emotional_truth: Reassurance is not always a sentence. Sometimes it is tone, proximity, a lowered fan, a refilled glass, and staying ordinary on purpose.
candidates.relatable_trigger: Couples where one person reads every small quietness as danger, and the other has learned that 'no' only lands when the whole room stops feeling like proof against it.
candidates.visual_evidence: Aachu alone on the bed with her phone lit; three tiny message drafts or erased words; Zuv in another frame quietly turning down the harsh tube light, bringing tea, sitting on the floor by the bed instead of hovering; the final frame can be just two hands around one cup.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: High if reduced to 'overthinking girl, patient boy.' Needs mutual tenderness and no joke at her expense; his quietness should also be shown as tired or distracted, not villainous.

candidates.title: Packed For Your Storms
candidates.one_line_concept: The fear is 'am I hard to handle?' and the answer is a bag full of unromantic evidence: hair tie, extra shawl, water, painkiller, charger, snack, all packed before Aachu even asks.
candidates.emotional_truth: Being loved by someone observant can make your needs feel less like a performance and more like part of the route.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The partner who knows the exact tiny things that prevent a meltdown: the seat away from the speaker, the backup snack, the 'we can leave early' look.
candidates.visual_evidence: A flat lay of Zuv's bag before they leave; Aachu shown later using one item without ceremony; a noisy public place in one frame and then a quieter corner; Zuv does not need to be in every slide because the packed objects already testify.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium. A care-kit can become Pinterest romance unless the items are oddly specific, slightly inconvenient, and clearly tied to real couple memory rather than aesthetic coziness.

candidates.title: The Last Bite Audit
candidates.one_line_concept: Aachu worries she is 'not enough' because she cannot be effortless, but Zuv notices the one daily proof everyone else misses: she saves him the best bite even on days she feels impossible.
candidates.emotional_truth: People who feel hard to love often keep loving in tiny, almost invisible ways while apologizing for needing anything back.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The couple habit where the best bite, the corner piece, the mango cheek, or the last spoon of dessert silently belongs to the other person.
candidates.visual_evidence: A plate with one perfect bite pushed to the side; Aachu alone at the table looking tired, not performatively sad; later Zuv finding the saved bite under a small inverted bowl or napkin; the tenderness is in the untouched food, not in a hug.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium-high if it becomes 'she is selfless, he appreciates her.' It needs the contradiction: she thinks she is not enough while her love has been sitting on the plate in plain sight.

candidates.title: The Exit Plan He Doesn't Make A Thing
candidates.one_line_concept: The question is 'am I not worth the risk?' and the behavior is Zuv quietly building exits into every plan so Aachu can come along without pretending to be easy.
candidates.emotional_truth: Real safety is not someone promising they will never leave. It is someone making it possible for you to leave the room and still belong to the day.
candidates.relatable_trigger: The partner who checks where the quieter table is, keeps the cab app open, stands between you and the crowd, and says 'we can go' before you have to beg.
candidates.visual_evidence: A busy cafe, wedding, or street scene; Aachu's hand at the edge of the frame near her bag strap; Zuv's phone with a cab route ready but unsent; a quieter staircase landing with two cups; some slides can show only crowd, phone, door, and hands.
candidates.risk_of_being_generic: Medium. The 'anxious girl rescued by calm boy' trap is close. It works only if Zuv is not a savior and Aachu is not helpless; the story is about shared planning, not extraction.

top_pick.title: The Chair Outside The Door
top_pick.reason: It gives the premise a behavior instead of a speech. It lets one slide be almost entirely Aachu, another be almost entirely objects, and still makes Zuv's love visible through restraint. The question 'am I hard to understand?' lands because the answer is not 'no, you're perfect'; it is 'I know when not to knock.'

rejected_patterns.pattern: Sad portrait plus direct question text
rejected_patterns.reason: The concept references already do this. Repeating it would be mood, not Aachu/Zuv behavior.

rejected_patterns.pattern: Every slide contains both partners facing each other
rejected_patterns.reason: It would force romance into frames where absence, objects, and traces can say more.
Too one-sided and too internet-worn. The idea must show care without making Aachu the problem or Zuv the saint.

rejected_patterns.pattern: Grand answer to 'am I hard to love?'
rejected_patterns.reason: A big reassurance line will feel like a quote card. The answer has to be in a glass, a chair, a charger, a saved bite, a cab route.

risk_notes: Do not copy the dark, theatrical, foreign visual language of the concept images; they are premise references only.
The strongest lane is quiet behavioral proof, not sadness aesthetics.
The risk across the room is gendered emotional labor: avoid making Zuv endlessly saintly or Aachu endlessly difficult.
These candidates are not prompts and do not lock slide count, exact text, or image generation.
